FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Documentation and Information Sectional Committee had been approved by the Management and Systems Division Council. Various forms of making entries in a Directory of Periodicals are in use. By bringing out this standard, effort has been made to harmonize making entries in directory of periodicals with a view to facilitate retrieval and exchange of information about periodicals.

IS 15282:2003

Indian Standard ENTRIES IN A DIRECTORY

At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate and apply the most recent editions of these standards: 1S No. 18: 1999/ 1s04 :1997 Title Information and documentation -- Rules for the abbreviation of title words and titles of publications ( third revision) Recommendation for frequency notation for periodical publications Guide for international standard serial numbering ( lSSN ) 3.1.4 Key title starting with numeric form is to be rendered as such, but its alphanumeric sequence is determined based on spelling out the numbers. Examples 1) 3D Education 2) 2001 The former is to be alphbetised as, Three D Education, whereas the latter as, Two thousand and one for alphabetical sequence. 3.1.5 In case title has various sections/parts/ supplements, etc then they are to be kept as a part of the main title, but are shown separately. Examples 1) Indian Journal Section A 2) Indian Journal Section B Similarly 1) Proceedings of Indian National Academy -- Part A. 2) Proceedings of Indian National Academy -- Part B. 3.2 Parallel or Variant Title or Alternate Science of Chemistry -- does not cover for making

It is derived from the title information appearing in the publication at the time of registration. Articles appearing in the beginning of the title shall be dropped. 3.1.2 When the information on the title source includes a generic term, such as bull@ in, technical bulletin, journal, transactions, proceedings, newsletter and report or its equivalent in other languages, and that generic term is linguistically separated from the issuing body, the key title should be rendered as in the generic term followed by the name of the issuing body. The generic term is separated from the name of the issuing body by a space hypen space. 1 OF ENTRIES

Title

Whenever an alternative title occurs it has to be mentioned for identification. Acronym title, titles in different languages or scripts are examples. These provide additional access points for search.

IS 15282:2003 3.3 Previous Title 3.5 Year and Volume Number Both the year of commencement and volume number of publication shall be given if available, so as to indicate approximate age of the periodical. Any change in the volume serial shall also be indicated suitably. 3.6 Frequency 3.4 Language Language may be represented by a code. If a periodical is published in more than one language, all the language codes shall be mentioned and defined. Distinction should not be made between mother language code and additional language code. Examples Yojna and India Today are published in multiple languages. Their language codes are mentioned as follows: a) b) Yojna eng, bin, tam, --3.8 Country of Publication India Today eng, bin, --Indian languages are Country of publication shall be given by a two letter code as given in IS 14836 ( Part 1 ). 3.9 Sponsoring Body Language codes for different given below: S1 No. i) ii) iii) iv) v) vi) vii) viii) ix) x) xi) xii) xiii) xiv) xv) xvi) xvii) xviii) xix) xx) xxi) Language Assamese Bengali English French German Gujarati Hindi Italian Kannada Kashmiri Malayalam Marathi Oriya Punjabi Russian Sanskrit Sindhi Spanish Tamil Telgu Urdu Frequency of a periodical shall be indicated as per IS 6666, for example, number of issues per year, that is, 6/12 means six issues in a year. 3.7 Subscription Rate

If a title has previous history, for example, change in title, merger with another title or splitting from a title, continuation of previous title, successor title or resumption of earlier title, the individual titles shall be appropriately recorded alongwith cross references, linking these titles.

Latest annual subscription price shall be given. Prices shall be given in the currency of the country of origin. The terms of availability of periodical shall also be indicated. For example, aspects such as, free to members, special subscription for students, etc, need to be presented.

@J

Many periodicals are controlled by a sponsoring organization. Name of the sponsoring body, wherever available shall be given in circular brackets, if it does not occur in continuation of the title proper on the title page. This may be a name of a Society, Association or Institute. In case ofjoint sponsors of any periodical, not more than two names shall be given and cross references shall be provided for other sponsors. 3.10 Publisher's Name and Address of the publisher shall be acquisition. 3.14 Circulation If a publisher provides circulation figures the same may be given. If circulation is restricted the same shall be indicated by `restricted'. 3.15 Saie of Periodicals If the marketing rights have not been given to any agent and it is done exclusively by the publisher or the sponsor, the information shall be appropriately indicated as `Supplied by ........................./Marketed by ........................... . 3.16 Form of Availability Number of periodicals are being made available in electronic form. Information regarding whether the periodical is available in any other form, for example, microfilm, microfiche, CD-ROM, online, etc, in full text or otherwise shall be appropriately indicated. 3.17 ISSN ( International Standard Serial Number)

International Standard Serial Number, a unique identification number assigned to a serial title by national centres under the auspices of International Serials Data Systems ( ISDS ) shall be given. This entry shall conform to 1S 10101. 3.18 Referred Periodical

Brief description of periodicals is

Many periodicals are reviewed and evaluated to maintain the quality of scholarly materials published and if this information is provided by the publisher, the same may be indicated by a symbol or notation. Symbol or notation to be used shall be defined in the directory. 3.19 Classification and Subject Heading

Class numbers shall be based on a standard scheme of classification and subject headings may be based on a thesaurus or subject heading list or any subject indexing system. The classification and subject heading system used shall be indicated in the directory.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications maybe reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), 131S. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards : Monthly Additions'.
